title: Pashto to English: First Steps

languagePolicy.existingGuide: src/ustad/pashtoLocale.js and locales/ps.js in ENGLISH OSTAD; no separate approved guide supplied.
languagePolicy.register: Short everyday phrases; polite plural تاسو / وکړئ matching the existing guide; familiar school/household vocabulary; no Afghan-register substitution.
languagePolicy.romanPashto: Optional parent reading aid only; never English phonics pronunciation.

scopeDecisions: Alphabet browsing is A–Z; sound lessons follow a systematic sound order. Starting with alphabetical A,B,C is not required for blending.

No untaught correspondences applies to independent reading/spelling and scored tasks. Oral modeled picture words and letter names necessarily contain later sounds. Picture labels remain hidden until decodable or explicitly taught as an exception/name. This interpretation requires Phase 1 approval.
The English lesson titles, objectives and comprehension-question glosses are authoring metadata. Child instructions/questions are Pashto; learner English print is explicitly listed practice content.
The core course is cumulative, not a claim to cover all English spelling. Unlisted words are excluded from independent texts until introduced.

No finite multiple-choice check can make chance success mathematically impossible. Gate on correct first responses and constructed output, use fresh retry forms, and flag repeated guessing; do not count watching/tapping Continue as mastery.

progressionDesign.continueLearning: First unfinished activity in the first unlocked unfinished lesson; restore its in-activity cursor and committed answers.
progressionDesign.checkpointTiming: Persist locally after every accepted interaction and activity commit, before changing activity. Resume paused; replay current short instruction from the start. Never auto-submit an unfinished answer.
progressionDesign.storage: Proposed IndexedDB transaction + durable sync outbox; retain existing profile identifiers and storage migration. Phase 2 storage implementation is not yet authorised.
progressionDesign.sync: Retry idempotent events on reconnection; remote account/provider is undecided. Anonymous offline use remains supported. Never silently replace newer per-activity work.

unlockGate.afterSecondError: Model the answer, mark that item assisted, then use a fresh independent item.
unlockGate.onFailure: Keep locked; provide targeted extra practice, then a fresh five-item check. No lost lives.

progressionDesign.replays: Completed lessons remain replayable; deduplicate mastery points by learner + content version + lesson ID.
progressionDesign.parentArea: Existing parent gate; placement probes start below proposed entry, assess letters/blending/spelling/phrases/reading, require 80% unassisted with constructed responses. Parent records a placement decision; a class selector alone is not proof of mastery.

interactionDesign.lowEndAndroid: Lazy-load illustrations/audio; 2D character default on constrained devices, pause offscreen animation, cap animation resolution; no lesson logic tied to frame rate.
interactionDesign.reducedMotion: Static worked example; do not remove explanations or assessment.
interactionDesign.speaking: Optional repeat-and-record for comparison; no automatic pronunciation pass without a validated recogniser or caregiver review.
interactionDesign.tracing: TapDots or letter selection equivalent; never gate literacy on fine motor ability.

audioDesign.policy: One central owner for all English and Pashto clips; new playback cancels the previous clip and invalidates callbacks. Global mute and replay on every instruction. Separate Pashto help button.
audioDesign.pureSounds: Record trained-speaker phonemes. Never synthesize phonemes by reading IPA or muh/suh/tuh. Stop consonants clipped; /m/ and /s/ may be sustained. /x/ and /qu/ letter patterns each represent two phonemes.
audioDesign.alignment: Recording-delivered word/phoneme boundaries drive highlighting and sliding letters. Timestamps remain null until recorded and reviewed; no fabricated synchronization.
audioDesign.englishAccent: One consistent rhotic accent: r after a vowel is always sounded (car, farm, park, water, here, are). bath is read with short a, like cat. Accept intelligible regional variants from children.
audioDesign.captions: Target word/sentence text remains visible; pure-sound cues use graphemes, not child-facing IPA.

reviewChecklist: Native English reviewer checks every sound-to-spelling mapping, article/pronoun pronunciation, sentence and literal answer key.
Trained phonics reviewer checks cumulative independent word lists, pure consonants, two oo sounds, two th sounds, x/qu sequences, adjacent consonants and split digraphs.
Lower Dir native reviewer checks every Pashto line for child comprehension, local vocabulary, respectful plural register, natural delivery and text direction.
Review Ali/Ayesha pronunciation with local families; do not impose one universal pronunciation.
Confirm pictures distinguish meanings; do not teach a word only by guessing from its picture.
Check goals, prerequisites, all five check items, correct answers and meaningful fresh retry forms for every lesson.
Record and sign off every English/Pashto clip, check no added schwa and align every read-along/phoneme sequence.
Test children with low English exposure; observe accessibility alternatives and the 5–8 minute session target.
Phase 2 reviewers must test all acceptance criteria on low-end Android, interrupted/offline sessions, mute and rapid repeated taps.
All content/audio/assets remain pending review until named reviewers sign dated fields; no automatic status promotion.
